answers.question: How do the frontend apps talk to the OpenMRS backend, REST or FHIR? Show me where each is used in the patient management app.

paragraphs.text: The frontend apps use **both**, but not equally. The everyday work — reading and writing patients, encounters, visits, queues, appointments, beds — goes over OpenMRS's own **REST API** (the `/ws/rest/v1` web services). A small, clearly bounded set of reads goes over **FHIR** (the R4 API exposed by the FHIR2 module), and it is almost entirely `Location` lookups plus a few `Patient`/`Encounter`/`Observation` reads. So: REST is the default, FHIR is the exception.
## The two access tokens
Both APIs are reached through the same helper, `openmrsFetch`, imported from the shared `@openmrs/esm-framework` package. What changes is the URL prefix, which comes from two framework constants:

| Constant | API | Typical path |
|---|---|---|
| `restBaseUrl` | OpenMRS REST web services | `/ws/rest/v1/...` |
| `fhirBaseUrl` | FHIR R4 (FHIR2 module) | `/ws/fhir2/R4/...` |

Because these come from the framework, the actual string values live outside this repository (in `openmrs-esm-core`), and I could not read them here — but the paths built on them (`/concept/...`, `/Location?...`) are unambiguous. The `_summary`, `_count`, `_tag`, `_include:iterate` query parameters in the FHIR calls are standard FHIR search syntax, which confirms the FHIR side.
## FHIR usage in the patient management app
There are only five places that import `fhirBaseUrl` in the whole repository.

**1. Location search in patient search** — the "refine search" panel fetches locations from FHIR and combines them with REST calls for concepts and person attribute types in the same file [1]. This file is the clearest illustration of the mixing: `useLocations` builds `${fhirBaseUrl}/Location?` [2], while `useAttributeConceptAnswers` uses `${restBaseUrl}/concept/...` [3] and `usePersonAttributeType` uses `${restBaseUrl}/personattributetype/...` [4].
**2. Queue locations in the service queues app** — `useQueueLocations` lists locations tagged "queue location" via FHIR [5].

**3. Location ancestry** — `useSessionLocationAncestry` walks the FHIR `Location.partOf` chain using `_include:iterate`, with a fallback to the location itself when the server does not support it [6].
**4. Ward location picker** — the ward app's `useLocations` uses `fhirBaseUrl` with a paginated FHIR hook [7].

**5. Patient lookup for a cohort** — after fetching cohort members over REST, the patient list app resolves their demographics with a FHIR `Patient/_search` POST and reads `result.data.entry` [8]. Note the cohort list call itself is REST, against the cohort module's `cohortm` endpoint [9].

Three of these FHIR hooks are not even hand-rolled `openmrsFetch` calls — they use the framework's FHIR-aware hooks `useFhirFetchAll` and `useFhirPagination`, which handle FHIR paging bundles for you.
## REST usage
REST is everywhere else, spread across all the app's packages. Typical examples:

- Registering a patient: `savePatient`, `saveEncounter`, `generateIdentifier`, `saveRelationship`, and identifier/name/attribute writes all POST to `${restBaseUrl}/...` [10]; the registration metadata lookups (address template, identifier types, ID generation options) are REST too [11].
- Clinical records in the ward app: creating an encounter, deleting an encounter, and the EmrApi configuration fetch are all REST [12].
- Queue entries: reads and mutations against `${restBaseUrl}/queue-entry`, `${restBaseUrl}/visit-queue-entry`, `${restBaseUrl}/queueutil/...` [13] and [14].
- Appointments, visits, beds, providers, concepts, system settings — all REST, e.g. appointments [15] and bed management [16].
## Why it is split this way

The pattern is deliberate, not accidental. FHIR is used where its search semantics are genuinely better: the ward app paginates large location lists through FHIR bundles [7], and `Location.partOf` traversal [17] has no clean REST equivalent. Everything else stays on REST because the custom representations (`v=custom:(...)`), the OpenMRS-specific endpoints (cohortm, idgen, emrapi, queue, bed) have no FHIR mapping, and REST is what the framework's `openmrsFetch` and the broader O3 codebase already standardised on.

```mermaid
---
title: How the patient management app reaches the backend
---
flowchart TD
  UI[React components and hooks] --> Fetch["openmrsFetch from esm-framework"]
  Fetch --> Rest["restBaseUrl - OpenMRS REST"]
  Fetch --> Fhir["fhirBaseUrl - FHIR R4"]
  Rest --> RestRes["patient, encounter, visit, queue, bed, appointment, concept, cohortm, idgen, emrapi"]
  Fhir --> FhirRes["Location search and partOf, Patient _search, Encounter, Observation"]
  FhirRes --> FhirHooks["useFhirFetchAll and useFhirPagination"]
```
## The same split elsewhere in the picked repositories
It is a product-wide convention, not a patient-management quirk:

- **Billing app** builds everything on REST — `apiBasePath` is `${restBaseUrl}/billing/` [18]; I found no `fhirBaseUrl` usage there.
- **Form engine lib** mixes them in one file: encounters, concepts, locations, forms, program enrolments, identifiers and person attributes over REST [19], with FHIR for the latest encounter and observations [20].
## What I could not verify

I could not read the literal values of `restBaseUrl` and `fhirBaseUrl`, since `@openmrs/esm-framework` is an installed dependency and not part of these repositories; the `/ws/rest/v1` and `/ws/fhir2/R4` paths above are the standard OpenMRS ones and are consistent with the endpoint segments in the code. The REST grep output was truncated at 200 matches across 65 files, so I counted only the FHIR usages exhaustively (a complete list of 10 matches in 5 files); the REST list is representative rather than a full inventory.
